hint.label: Vocabulary

cats.sound: As a dedicated breeder, I focus on health-testing dog parents for genetic issues and carefully screening buyers to ensure my puppies thrive in loving, suitable homes. This work preserves vital breed standards—like temperament and size—while providing families with predictable companions.

All breeding, even responsible, fuels pet overpopulation and illnesses in breeds. At the same time millions of healthy animals are euthanized in shelters each year. Please adopt instead to save lives and stop over breeding! Shelters have wonderful, often healthier mixed breeds ready for forever homes.

I find ethical breeding has its place, but believe that we should reform breeding through strict licensing and bans on profit-driven high-volume operations. Pair this with breeder fees to finance shelters for better care, no-kill goals, and transparent adoptions. Not everyone is capable to provide for shelter dogs with unknown histories, so the idea to adopt or shop responsibly could unite us against unethical breeders while strengthening shelters.

Breeding leads to overpopulation and furthers health issues in breeds.
Shelter animals are often healthier than standardised breeds.
More adoption saves pets from euthanisation.
Breeding needs to be reformed through strict licensing of breeders.
Shelters need to be better supported financially so they may provide better care.
Breeder fees could be used to support pet shelters.
